Balestier

Balestier 49

  1. Must see · Hawker & Zi Char · Balestier

    Balestier Road Hoover Rojak

    The long-famous Balestier rojak, now at Whampoa Food Centre and a repeat Michelin Bib Gourmand pick — a killer sauce of assam, fermented prawn paste and sugar tossed with crunchy jellyfish and creamy century egg alongside the usual fruit, you tiao and tau pok.

    Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-06, Singapore 320090

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Time Out Singapore, HungryGoWhere, Eatbook.sg

  2. Must see · Bak Kut Teh & Soups · Balestier

    Beach Road Fish Head Bee Hoon

    Held the Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025, and widely called one of Singapore's best fish soups: sliced or fried fish-head bee hoon in a rich, milky stock finished with fried garlic. Morning hours only, a few days a week — go early.

    Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-46, Singapore

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  3. Must see · Balestier

    Goh Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple & Wayang Stage

    Balestier's red temple, founded in 1847 by Hokkien labourers on Joseph Balestier's sugar-cane estate ('Goh Chor' = Rochore), rebuilt in southern Chinese style in 1920/1928 — and beside it one of Singapore's last permanent wayang (Chinese opera) stages, built 1906 by Tan Boo Liat and still used by troupes during the Hungry Ghost Festival. Conserved by URA.

    Look for Temple + 1906 opera stage; performances in the 7th lunar month

    249 Balestier Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Remember Singapore, Urban Redevelopment Authority

  4. Must see · Balestier

    Former Malay Film Productions Studio (Shaw Studio)

    Shaw Brothers' Malay Film Productions studio on Jalan Ampas (1947-1969), where more than 150 films — many starring P. Ramlee — were shot in the golden age of Malay cinema. The surviving studio gate and buildings sit at the end of a quiet lane off Balestier Road.

    Look for Heritage site — exterior only; on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail

    8 Jalan Ampas, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, TheSmartLocal, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

  5. Must see · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Balestier

    Loy Kee Best Chicken Rice

    Balestier's other chicken-rice institution (alongside Boon Tong Kee): founded in 1953 by Hainanese immigrants and run by three generations, everything made from scratch — silky steamed or crisp-skinned roast chicken over fluffy rice cooked in garlicky chicken broth, with chilli, dark soy and ginger paste. The Loy Kee Special Set is the full Hainanese spread on one tray.

    342 Balestier Road, Singapore 329774

    Recommended by Time Out Singapore, Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  6. Must see · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Balestier

    Loong Fatt Tau Sar Piah

    Balestier is Singapore's tau sar piah street, and Loong Fatt (since 1948) is its original — still in the same shophouse with the old tiled walls and floor, wooden tables and booths, baking flaky mung-bean pastries by hand. A stop on the National Heritage Board's Balestier Food Trail.

    639 Balestier Road, Singapore 329922

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Eatbook.sg, TRAVELLERAU

  7. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Balestier

    Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee

    You see the queue before the stall: a Michelin Bib Gourmand (2023) fried Hokkien mee that pairs thick bee hoon with yellow noodles in a slightly wet, umami-laden prawn stock. Open from mid-afternoon into the small hours, it is Whampoa's night-market anchor.

    Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-32, Singapore 320090

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), HungryGoWhere

  8. Must see · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Balestier

    Boon Tong Kee (Balestier)

    A chicken rice institution since 1979; promoted to Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.

    399/401/403 Balestier Road

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary, AsiaOne

  9. Must see · Balestier

    Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall

    Wan Qing Yuan, the 1880s villa off Balestier Road that Dr Sun Yat Sen used as his Southeast Asian base for the Tongmenghui — now a National Monument whose galleries tell how overseas Chinese communities bankrolled and shaped the 1911 Revolution. Anchor stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

    Look for National Monument & museum; Tue-Sun, ticketed

    12 Tai Gin Road, Singapore 327874

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), WONDERWALL

  10. Must see · Balestier

    Maha Sasana Ramsi Burmese Buddhist Temple

    Singapore's Burmese Buddhist temple, founded on Kinta Road in 1878 and rebuilt beside the Sun Yat Sen villa on Tai Gin Road in 1991 — it houses the largest white-marble Buddha outside Myanmar, carved from a single block of Mandalay marble. On the 'Faith, Film and Food' route of NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail.

    Look for Buddhist temple; free; dress modestly

    14 Tai Gin Road, Singapore 327873

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), WONDERWALL

  11. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Balestier

    Amoy St Lor Mee (Best Lu Mian In Town)

    Whampoa is almost synonymous with this stall and its bold claim to the 'Best Lu Mian In Town': a two-item menu of thick, starchy lor mee laden with ngoh hiang, fish nuggets and braised pork (or the amped-up Jumbo Meal), with long morning queues.

    Whampoa Makan Place, 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-19, Singapore

    Recommended by TheSmartLocal, Daniel Food Diary, City Nomads (Singapore city guide), HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui

  12. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Deep Fried Carrot Cake (Whampoa)

    A morning-only stall (about 6.30am to 12.30pm, Tue-Sun) deep-frying radish cake until crisp outside and soft within — in City Nomads', Eatbook's, TheSmartLocal's and HungryGoWhere's Whampoa guides. Its owner Mr Lim has sold carrot cake in stick form for over two decades (Women's Weekly).

    Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, #01-36, Singapore (block to confirm)

    Recommended by City Nomads (Singapore city guide), Eatbook.sg, TheSmartLocal, HungryGoWhere, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  13. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Liang Zhao Ji Duck Rice

    A former Michelin Bib Gourmand (2017) braised-duck stall: soy duck rice drenched in gravy, but regulars come for the velvety Cantonese-style duck porridge with a splash of braising gravy — 'you have never tasted duck porridge this good' (Miss Tam Chiak).

    Whampoa Makan Place, 90 Whampoa Drive, #01-07, Singapore 320090

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak, City Nomads (Singapore city guide), HungryGoWhere

  14. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Bao Er Cafe (Balestier Plaza)

    The viral hole-in-the-wall on Balestier Plaza's second floor: wok-kissed Hokkien mee and homemade kaya toast that Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost: 'local breakfast done right') and Miss Tam Chiak have all written up — it has since spawned outlets in Holland Village (Jun 2025) and Fortune Centre (Dec 2025).

    Balestier Plaza (level 2), 400 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary

  15. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Balestier

    Niu Dian Beef Noodles (VIIO @ Balestier)

    The Taipei beef-noodle shop recognised by the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand in Taipei opened its first overseas outlet here on 13 Feb 2023 — a modern take on Taiwanese braised beef noodles (Seth Lui, Eatbook, Miss Tam Chiak, HungryGoWhere).

    VIIO @ Balestier, 520 Balestier Road, Singapore (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak, HungryGoWhere

  16. Worth the detour · Balestier

    Balestier Market

    The sole surviving rural-market building in Singapore, designed by local architect Kwan Yow Luen with animal-and-flower reliefs across its cream walls — a heritage-trail stop that still trades as a cluster of eateries. A planned April 2025 closure was reversed — the tenancy was extended by two years (Seth Lui, Feb 2025).

    Look for Heritage market building; eateries

    411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), WONDERWALL, Seth Lui

  17. Worth the detour · Balestier

    Whampoa Makan Place

    The 1973 hawker centre and wet market spread across HDB blocks 90, 91 and 92 on Whampoa Drive — successor to the old Rayman Market and a stop on NHB's Balestier Heritage Trail. Two cooked-food halls side by side hold some of Balestier's best breakfasts: Hoover rojak, fish-head bee hoon, lor mee, Hokkien mee.

    Look for Hawker centre & wet market; most stalls morning to mid-afternoon

    Blocks 90-92 Whampoa Drive, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB), TheSmartLocal

  18. Worth the detour · Balestier

    Whampoa Dragon Fountain

    A 1973 dragon sculpture clad in broken China rice bowls, built as the centrepiece of a playground park behind Block 85 Whampoa; the park was cleared for the CTE in 1985 and the fountain stopped running after the 1980s, but the weathered dragon still coils by the expressway — one of Singapore's few surviving 1970s HDB-estate landmarks.

    Look for Free; outdoor sculpture

    Whampoa Drive (near Block 85), Whampoa, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Remember Singapore, TheSmartLocal

  19. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Balestier

    Bee Kia Seafood Restaurant

    A long-running zi char stall in the corner of a Balestier Hill coffeeshop, famous for its beef hor fun — silky rice-noodle sheets and tender beef in a fragrant black-bean gravy loaded with wok hei — the subject of Dr Leslie Tay's 'beef hor fun challenge'. Prawn paste chicken is the other order. Reviewers note consistency depends on who is at the wok.

    1 Thomson Road, #01-326, Balestier Hill Shopping Centre, Singapore 320002

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak

  20. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Kai Juan (Ah Hak) Bak Kut Teh

    Half a century of Teochew-style bak kut teh — a clear, moderately peppery broth over pork ribs, with rice and salted vegetables for about $7.50 — in a coffeeshop of rusty gates, granite floors and wooden tables that still looks 1970s. A stop on NHB's Balestier Food Trail.

    Kai Juan Coffeeshop, 395/397 Balestier Road, Singapore (exact unit to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  21. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Guang Dong Xiao Shi (Whampoa)

    Yong tau foo served in laksa gravy (about $4) — a Whampoa crossover named by City Nomads, TheSmartLocal and Seth Lui.

    Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-21, Singapore 320091

    Recommended by City Nomads (Singapore city guide), TheSmartLocal, Seth Lui

  22. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Balestier

    Lam Yeo Coffee Powder Factory

    A family coffee roaster since 1950 selling Nanyang-style kopi powder — beans from Indonesia roasted the traditional way with sugar and margarine (the Legacy Blend keeps the founding recipe). On NHB's Balestier Food Trail; Makansutra profiled its revival.

    328 Balestier Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Makansutra

    Whampoa Soya Bean & Grass Jelly Drinks

    A second-generation stall in the same spot since 1979 (family business from 1968), making silky tau huay and soya milk — written up by Dr Leslie Tay ('smooth as silk') and Daniel Food Diary, and named in City Nomads' Whampoa guide; DFD notes its inclusion in the MICHELIN Guide.

    Whampoa Makan Place, Block 91 Whampoa Drive, #01-52, Singapore 320091

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), City Nomads (Singapore city guide)

  24. Worth the detour · Balestier

    Balestier Art Deco Shophouses

    1950s Art Deco blocks built over former taro farmland and ponds, unusual among shophouses in housing a separate apartment on each floor — streamlined façades conserved with the pre-war shophouses along Balestier Road in 2003.

    Look for Conserved streetscape — view from Balestier Road

    230 & 246 Balestier Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

    Huat Heng Fried Oyster

    Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore — stall unit to confirm at geocode

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Eatbook.sg

  35. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Whampoa Keng Fish Head Steamboat (Balestier)

    The Balestier flagship of Whampoa Keng, famous for charcoal fish-head steamboat in a rich broth plus zi char dishes — chronicled by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost: the 'one man, two wives' story and the new flagship) and reviewed again by Live2Makan in Aug 2025.

    556 Balestier Road, Singapore

  36. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Balestier Bak Kut Teh (Kian Lian)

    A 24-hour bak kut teh house run by three generations of the Yap family since 1966; whole blocks of sugarcane go into the peppery Teochew broth — a nod to Balestier's sugar-plantation past. On Seth Lui's 18 best bak kut teh (Oct 2024) and Eatbook's best bak kut teh list.

    365/369 Balestier Road, Singapore 329785

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  37. Deep cut · Balestier

    Shaw Plaza (former Hoover Theatre site)

    Where Shaw Organisation's Hoover Theatre (opened 1960 at the Jalan Ampas junction, a cinema, live-show stage and even a church over 36 years) stood beside the President Theatre — both demolished in 1996 for today's Shaw Plaza-Twin Heights (1999), whose Balestier Cineplex kept the area's film thread alive; the Malay Film Productions studio is just down Jalan Ampas.

    Look for Mall & cinema site

    360 Balestier Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NLB Singapore Infopedia, Remember Singapore

    Nyonya Chendol (Whampoa)

    Shaved ice, pandan jelly, coconut milk and gula Melaka — the Whampoa chendol named by both Eatbook and HungryGoWhere.

    Whampoa Makan Place, Whampoa Drive, Singapore (unit to confirm)

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui

  39. Deep cut · Balestier

    Balestier Point

    An 18-storey 1986 apartment block whose stacked, Lego-like cubic modules — each home with its own terrace — were inspired by Moshe Safdie's Habitat 67 in Montreal: Balestier's modernist landmark, seen from the street.

    Look for Modernist residential landmark — view from outside

    Balestier Road, Singapore (to confirm at geocode)

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), WONDERWALL

  40. Deep cut · Balestier

    Zhongshan Park

    A small green with an open lawn and pond, named for Dr Sun Yat Sen (Sun Zhongshan) — it faces the villa where he stayed, now the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.

    Look for Neighbourhood park

    Ah Hood Road / Jalan Rajah, Balestier, Singapore

    Recommended by Little Day Out, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

  41. Deep cut · Balestier

    Balestier Plain & Ceylon Sports Club

    The open playing fields where five community clubs — the Indian Association, YMCA, Ceylon Sports Club and others — have shared grounds since the 1920s; the Ceylon Sports Club (est. 1928 from the 1920 Lanka Union) has its clubhouse here. Used as a Japanese Occupation vehicle dump, re-turfed by the clubs after 1945.

    Look for Club grounds — view from Balestier Road

    101 Balestier Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), NLB Singapore Infopedia

  49. Closed — kept for the record · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Balestier

    Miao Sin Popiah & Carrot Cake — CLOSED

    CLOSED 26 Feb 2026. Ong Chin Quay's 45-year-old popiah and carrot-cake stall (started 1980 on Upper Boon Keng Road, at Balestier Market since the 2010s) shut when the 72-year-old hawker found no successor (Mothership; Seth Lui). Women's Weekly had named it among Balestier Food Centre's best and Singapore's great popiah stops. Kept here, flagged, as part of the market's record.

    Balestier Market & Food Centre, 411 Balestier Road, Singapore 329930

    Recommended by Mothership, Seth Lui, The Singapore Women's Weekly

How this guide was made

Web-searched & fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, local news & magazines, and vetted local/viral creators — in data/sources.json. Coordinates are verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
